findings.claim: TRUNK-6682 carries the `backport` label, but the new API is tagged `@since 3.0.0` only (and the old injectMissingMetadata overload is `@Deprecated(since = "3.0.0")`), and the change uses Java 16+ syntax (`private record LoadedImage` at ImageHandler.java:153, pattern-matching `instanceof S3Exception s3Exception` at S3StorageService.java:178) that will not compile on the 2.8.x line, which builds at Java 1.8; is this meant to be backported to 2.8.x, and if so should it be written to Java 8 with the 2.8.x version added to each @since?
findings.evidence: Ticket JSON: labels [backport, community-priority, performance], fixVersions []. Ticket says the regression came with the 2.8.x storage abstraction. `git show a085b50b6^:pom.xml` (last 2.8.0-SNAPSHOT commit before 'Bump version to 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT') has <javaCompilerVersion>1.8</javaCompilerVersion> at line 1234. A throwaway P.java with a private record and a pattern instanceof: `javac --release 8` -> 'records are not supported in -source 8' and 'pattern matching in instanceof is not supported in -source 8' (exit 1); `--release 21` exit 0. StorageService.java:31 shows the convention of listing every line in @since (2.8.0, 2.7.5, 2.6.16, 2.5.15). This extends the still-open sub-point of the 2026-09-22 @since thread (comment 4070873955: 'plus whatever maintenance lines it gets backported to'), so it belongs as a reply there, not a new thread. Asked as a question because whether to backport is the maintainers' call.

verdict: Close to mergeable on master: every prior review thread is addressed at 86b96c7d6 and the targeted tests (78) pass with mutation probes showing they guard the new behaviour; the one open item is whether the backport-labelled ticket expects a 2.8.x version, which this code cannot be cherry-picked to as written.

Read the full main-code diff (StorageService, DataWithMetadata, LocalStorageService, S3StorageService, AbstractHandler, all five bundled handlers, messages.properties) and all test diffs. Checked each prior thread against the head: Greptile URI_VIEW metadata (fixed + test), AbstractMethodError (default method), record formatting (now a class), ibacher's shared internals/ordering comment/NoSuchFileException docs/Javadoc suggestion/parseDataKey API change (reverted), call-count question (now 1 exists + stat + open on local), ImageHandler legacy-title fallback (fixed + test), S3 multipart length (fixed + mock test), long Unicode legacy names (FileSystemException fallback + test with obs dir created), per-handler count tests, exists containment, S3 getData delegation, deprecation of the 2-arg overload, restored AbstractHandler count test, legacy getDataWithMetadata test (cdbc3b108, matches the suggestion verbatim). Step 2: the remaining handler-level exists() probe was argued and closed by ibacher (thread on AbstractHandler:127), so not reopened. Traced outward: git grep shows StorageService is used only in api (positive control: hits in api), getPath is now only used by purgeData, injectMissingMetadata callers all use the 3-arg form; reasoned through precedence flip (reads now current-first, purge still legacy-first) and judged a both-locations collision unrealistic given dated new-layout keys; compared legacy-layout op counts (equal to master by reasoning); checked exception-type changes in Text/BinaryData/BinaryStream handlers (still throw on a missing file, only type differs for non-missing I/O errors). Ran LocalStorageServiceTest, S3StorageServiceTest, AbstractHandlerTest and the five handler tests at head: 78 tests, 0 failures. Mutation probes: removing the legacy fallback in LocalStorageService.read turned 5 LocalStorageServiceTest tests red; adding a separate getMetadata call in TextHandler turned the TextHandler count test red. Both restored with git checkout. S3 not-found translation verified with a throwaway mocked-S3AsyncClient test (since deleted): a NoSuchKeyException 404 makes getDataWithMetadata, getData and getMetadata throw NoSuchFileException; a 403 S3Exception stays a plain IOException (2 tests green). Control: changing the 404 check to 999 turned the not-found test red; restored with git checkout.
